scenes.label: Meet Kabir
scenes.title: The fastest list on the field
scenes.caption: Meet Kabir. For Cyberpur School's sports day, he's built a live leaderboard. Each time a runner crosses the line, their time goes in, and the list sorts itself again, fastest first. He tested it with his class's thirty runners, and it was instant. Today, 2,000 runners from twelve schools will race, and Kabir can't wait.

He tested it with his class's thirty runners, and it was instant. Today, two thousand runners from twelve schools will race, and Kabir can't wait.
scenes.dialogue: Every finish time, sorted in a blink!

scenes.label: The freeze
scenes.title: Frozen at prize time
scenes.caption: By four o'clock, the results are pouring in. Then the leaderboard freezes. A little wheel spins and spins. The principal is waiting to announce the winners, and Coach Mehra keeps messaging: is the list ready? Kabir's face feels hot. With thirty runners, the code gave the right order in a blink. So why is it stuck now?
scenes.dialogue: It worked with thirty runners. Why is it stuck now?

scenes.label: Ask Ms Iyer
scenes.title: Same answer, different work
scenes.caption: Kabir calls Ms Iyer, his computer teacher. Together they read the code. His bubble sort compares neighbours and swaps them, pass after pass. For 2,000 runners, that's about two million comparisons, and it re-sorts after every new time. Merge sort splits the list into halves, sorts each half, then merges them in order. Its work grows roughly like n log n.

scenes.dialogue: So both sorts are right, but one works much harder?

scenes.label: Race the sorts
scenes.title: Predict, run, then choose
scenes.caption: Your turn. Help Kabir race the two sorts on three test lists: 8 results already in order, 100 in reverse, and all 2,000 mixed up. Before each race, predict which sort will make fewer comparisons, then run it and read the counters. Watch out: the winner can change with the list. Then choose the sort for sports day.

Before each race, predict which sort will make fewer comparisons, then run it and read the counters. Watch out: the winner can change with the list. Then choose the sort for sports day.
scenes.dialogue: Let's measure the work, not guess.

scenes.label: Why it grows
scenes.title: Time complexity: how work grows
scenes.caption: The counters show a pattern called time complexity: how an algorithm's work grows as its input grows. Bubble sort's comparisons grow like n², so twice the runners means about four times the work. Merge sort grows like n log n, just over double. On a tiny, tidy list, bubble sort's early stop can win. On big mixed lists, merge sort wins easily.

scenes.dialogue: Double the runners, and bubble sort does four times the work!

scenes.label: Prize time
scenes.title: Winners on the big screen
scenes.caption: Kabir switches the leaderboard to merge sort. Now each re-sort takes about twenty thousand comparisons instead of two million, and the list keeps up easily. The winners appear just in time, and Coach Mehra sends a thumbs up. Correct answers matter, but so does the work behind them. Your turn: help Kabir race the sorters on new lists!
scenes.dialogue: Merge sort for big lists. Measure before you guess!
